title: Switch-generation conjecture for the matching preorder
source: Joseph Briggs, Jessica McDonald and Songling Shan, “Degree sequences realizing labelled perfect matchings”, arXiv:2510.01110 (2025). https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01110
statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}_n$ be the set of the labelled perfect matchings under consideration, and let $\preceq$ be the preorder on this set. A **switch** is the local transformation defined earlier in the paper. **Switch-generation conjecture.** If $N,M\in\mathcal{M}_n$ satisfy $N\preceq M$, then there exists a sequence

$$
N=M_1\preceq M_2\preceq\dots\preceq M_{k-1}\preceq M_k=M
$$

such that $M_j$ is a switch of $M_{j+1}$ for every $j$. This is presented as an open conjecture about whether the preorder is generated by switches; the supplied parser gives no evidence of resolution.
summary: For perfect matchings N and M of the vertex set {1, ..., n}, write N ⪯ M when every weakly decreasing degree sequence that has a realization containing M also has one containing N. If N ⪯ M then there is a chain N = M_1 ⪯ M_2 ⪯ ... ⪯ M_k = M in which each step is one of the three switches of the source. This is Conjecture 11 of Briggs, McDonald and Shan. The proof shows that the preorder is the reverse Bruhat order on fixed-point-free involutions: a new separating-graph lemma produces, whenever a crossing-count inequality fails, a degree sequence realized with M but not with N; a direct induction on rank defects then moves from N toward M one switch at a time, and the source's Lemma 10(b) keeps every step inside the preorder. Lean defines matchings as edge sets, realizability by actual simple graphs with prescribed degrees, and the three switch types literally.
paste_summary: Proved. The preorder on perfect matchings defined by realizability of degree sequences is generated by switches: if N ⪯ M there is a chain of switches from N to M, each step respecting the preorder. This is Conjecture 11 of Briggs, McDonald and Shan; the preorder is the reverse Bruhat order on fixed-point-free involutions.
caveat: Bounded literature search only; the source exists as a single arXiv version with no journal reference. Only the separating-graph lemma is new: the rest uses the Bruhat rank criterion, a classical fact about covers of Bruhat order on fixed-point-free involutions (Watson 2014, here replaced by a direct rank-defect induction proved in Lean) and the source's own Lemma 10(b) (also proved in Lean). A specialist who knows the source's cut inequality may find the lemma natural (cross-model confidence: correct 0.93, novelty 0.88, first tier 0.6). Liu and Zeng, arXiv:2604.11939, prove a different conjecture of the same source. No second cross-model lane read the finished Lean: root compared the statement with the endpoint that reviewer had written, and the GPT-6.1 Sol final check compared the definitions with the source and by brute force for n = 4, 6, 8.
